title: Hue-shift ramps instead of straight value ramps
claim: Shadows should shift cooler/blue-purple and lights warmer/yellow across a colour ramp, not just change brightness; saturation should peak mid-ramp and drop at both ends.
project_relevance: Directly governs how we build our 16-colour env ramps and 48-colour hero ramp so materials don't look flat or clash scene-to-scene.

title: Pick an existing palette, swap later
claim: Palette choice shouldn't block starting work; pick a known 16/32-colour palette and swap it later since palette-swapping finished pixel art is cheap.
project_relevance: Lets background/sprite artists start Scene 01 assets now against a placeholder env palette without waiting on final colour lock.

title: Carry a restraint/simplicity aesthetic across projects, not a literal locked palette
claim: A studio can carry a deliberate visual-restraint/simplicity philosophy from a 2D game into a later 3D project rather than re-deriving the look from scratch; this is a studio-level aesthetic choice, not a documented literal locked palette reused as a brand asset.
project_relevance: Supports treating our 16-colour env / 48-colour hero budget as a house aesthetic to carry forward, but we should state our own hard lock as our decision, not cite this article as proof of one.

title: Full dark outline to lock silhouette, then selective outline
claim: Start with a full dark/black outline to lock the silhouette, then replace outline pixels with lighter/body-matched colours on the lit side, keeping dark line only against background and for internal segmentation.
project_relevance: Our hero outline strategy for the 48-colour hero palette; informs whether to add a selout pass on top of PixelLab's flat outline output.

title: PixelLab's outline param only exposed a flat full-outline mode in our tests
claim: Our hero v3 PixelLab calls used outline="single color black outline" on create-character-v3; no selective-outline value was exercised or found documented for this endpoint in the logs we inspected.
project_relevance: If selective outlining is wanted, we likely need a post-process pass over PixelLab output rather than relying on an API parameter.

title: One consistent light source, think in volumes
claim: Pick one light source (commonly front/above-left) and hold it constant across the whole sprite set; think in volumes/forms, not flat line-fills; squint-test for a few large light/dark clusters.
project_relevance: This is the core rule for our NW-lighting convention across floors, walls, props and hero.

title: Hybrid 2D/3D bump-map lighting on layered sprites
claim: Sprites split into parts, rebuilt in a 3D scene, hand-painted per-piece into a bump map so each part receives correct in-engine lighting — a hybrid 2D/3D pipeline rather than flat hand shading.
project_relevance: Out of scope for our budget/tooling (no 3D bump-map pipeline), but confirms flat hand-shading is a legitimate simpler alternative used by AA-scale studios too.

examples.what_to_look_at: Consistent directional shading on buildings/props across changing dawn/dusk lighting

title: Stair-stepped flat lighting ramp over a low-res render
claim: A Short Hike renders a full 3D world to a tiny offscreen texture and applies a custom unlit shader with a stair-stepped lighting ramp, deliberately flattening shading bands to stay crisp.
project_relevance: Not our pipeline (we're hand/AI-authored sprites, not a 3D-to-pixel render), but validates flattened/banded shading as an intentional readability choice at small scale.

examples.what_to_look_at: Stair-stepped shading bands on terrain and characters instead of smooth gradients

title: Over-lighting 2D sprites breaks the pixel-art read
claim: Octopath's team found flat 2D lighting insufficient on its own, added true 3D depth/DOF, but had to re-balance resolution/saturation because over-resolved/over-lit sprites lose their pixel-art appeal.
project_relevance: Caution against layering heavy dynamic lighting/post-fx onto our flat hero/env sprites; keep lighting simple and intentional.

examples.what_to_look_at: HD-2D sprites against a lit 3D diorama with shallow DOF

title: Only AA steps 2+ pixels long; never AA a 45° step
claim: Apply anti-aliasing only to staircase steps 2+ pixels long; never AA a 1x1/45-degree step or already-straight lines — that's the main cause of over-AA blur. AA run length should scale with step length.
project_relevance: Concrete rule for our pixel-art pass / any manual cleanup of PixelLab output edges.

title: Never AA the outer edge against an unknown background
claim: Don't anti-alias the outer edge of a sprite meant to sit on an unknown game background colour — AA tuned for one background colour looks wrong on another; AA inner edges only.
project_relevance: Directly applicable: our hero sprites are no_background PNGs composited over varying floor/wall tiles.

title: Dither large flat areas or rough textures, not everything
claim: Dithering fakes an intermediate shade with a noise pattern instead of a new palette colour; works best on large single-colour areas or rough/bumpy texture; some artists skip it entirely.
project_relevance: Optional technique for our wall/floor fills if flat colour reads too plain within the 16-colour env budget.

title: Fix banding via band compression or gradient-direction match
claim: Visible flat colour bands read as flat/blurry; fix via band compression (squeeze bands into a tiny area) or by rotating gradient/AA direction to match the surface slope.
project_relevance: QA checklist item for our floor/wall shading passes.

title: Edge-detect outline + distance fog compensates for low-res noise
claim: A Short Hike pairs a soft edge-detection outline pass with distance fog specifically to counter low-pixel-count noise at a distance.
project_relevance: A cheap readability fix if our Scene 01 interior ever needs far-background props at reduced detail.

examples.what_to_look_at: Soft outline on distant terrain fading into fog

title: Prototype shading/AA techniques large, then scale down
claim: Tutorials often demonstrate shading/AA/selout techniques on a larger canvas (e.g. 96x96) first because it's easier to see, then apply the same technique at the real small scale.
project_relevance: Workflow tip for sprite artists iterating on 128px-cell / 80-96px hero art before committing to final resolution.

title: Detail density must match canvas size
claim: Saint11 maintains dedicated 'Scaling Pixel Art' / 'Big Pixel Art' series specifically on detail-density tradeoffs at different canvas sizes.
project_relevance: Supports a fixed detail budget per asset tier (hero vs. prop vs. tile) rather than one density rule for everything.

title: Fix one small anchor prop's scale first, derive everything else from it
claim: Unpacking fixed the smallest drawable unit (a mug) first; all other props including tiny items scale/abstract relative to it rather than by true relative size.
project_relevance: Directly actionable: pick one small Scene 01 prop (e.g. a mug/book) as our scale anchor before drawing the rest of the prop set.

title: 2:1 pixel iso angle, not true 30° CAD isometric
claim: Pixel-art isometric uses a 2-pixel-across/1-pixel-down ratio (~26.565°); true 30° isometric looks jaggy at pixel scale. Tile-size guidance given: 32x16, 64x32, 128x64.
project_relevance: Confirms our 64x32 tile spec matches established pixel-iso convention exactly.

title: Overlapping wall vs one-wall-per-tile convention
claim: Two established iso-wall conventions: walls drawn slightly outside the tile boundary (needs 4 directional variants) vs. one wall occupying its own full tile (needs only 1 asset).
project_relevance: Direct input to our Scene 01 wall-tile asset count/budget decision.

examples.what_to_look_at: Overlapping wall style requiring directional variants

title: Documented iso-room pitfalls: ambient wall banding, floating objects, wall clipping
claim: The Sims' own design documentation lists concrete defects to avoid: ambient-only wall lighting bands at low light, objects without shadows appear to float, and multi-tile objects poke through walls.
project_relevance: Direct QA checklist for our wall/floor/prop art pass on Scene 01.

examples.what_to_look_at: Wall shading at low ambient light, object shadow treatment

title: Align body landmarks to the floor-plane diagonal
claim: All body landmarks (shoulders, hips, eyes, feet) sit on the same diagonal as the floor plane's iso angle so the character reads as standing on the grid; front/back pose covers all 4 cardinals via mirroring.
project_relevance: Directly applicable to our hero sprite's feet-anchor (64,127) and directional pose set.

examples.what_to_look_at: Chibi sprite landmark alignment to the iso floor diagonal

title: Flat-textured ground + perpendicular billboard quads for depth
claim: Flat-textured ground tiles with perpendicular 2D quads for grass/props deliver iso depth cues without true 3D geometry.
project_relevance: A cheap way to add vertical prop detail (rugs, plants) on our flat floor tiles without a 3D pipeline.

title: Shared modular furniture catalog on a fixed iso grid
claim: Habbo Hotel's rooms are built entirely from a shared library of interchangeable iso-aligned furniture pieces placed on a fixed grid.
project_relevance: Direct model for our prop system: a reusable iso-aligned prop catalog rather than one-off hand-placed art per room.

title: Keep iconic room layouts stable over time
claim: Long-lived public rooms (e.g. the Library) kept their furni layout/identity consistent across years, including a known quirk left in deliberately.
project_relevance: Supports locking Scene 01's apartment layout once set rather than redesigning it on every art pass.

title: Periodic style redraws keep long productions from looking dated
claim: D-Pad Studio redesigned and redrew Owlboy's art assets multiple times over a 10-year production specifically so the final game wouldn't look '10 years out of date'.
project_relevance: Budget expectation: our hero/env art may need at least one deliberate style pass later in production, not just an initial style guide.

title: PixelLab animate-with-text-v3 is the recommended default animation mode
claim: PixelLab's docs state 'v3' animation mode usually produces higher quality results than legacy 'pro' mode and is cheaper; 'pro' mode costs 10-25 generations per direction (80-200 for a full 8-direction set) on subscription.
project_relevance: Cost-critical: if/when we spend new PixelLab generations on hero animation, default to v3 mode to conserve the trial budget.

title: Heart Machine house vibrancy; flat-blocking-for-legibility is our hypothesis, not a sourced HLD claim
claim: Heart Machine (HLD's studio) describes a general house 'vibrancy' feel carried into their new game Possessor(s); the source does not make a specific claim that HLD itself commits to flat colour blocking over gradient shading for character legibility — that mechanism is our own hypothesis to test, not a documented HLD design fact.
project_relevance: A legibility option worth testing ourselves if our hero reads poorly against Scene 01's 16-colour env palette, but treat as our hypothesis, not an HLD-sourced fact.

title: Build interiors from a shared furniture catalog
claim: Habbo Hotel's rooms are entirely assembled from a shared library of interchangeable iso-aligned furniture pieces rather than bespoke room art.
project_relevance: Supports building a reusable prop/furniture atlas for Scene 01 (and future rooms) instead of one-off per-room art.

title: Give every prop a shadow or it floats
claim: The Sims' design documentation flags objects without shadows as appearing to float above the floor plane.
project_relevance: Hard requirement for every Scene 01 prop: a drop shadow or contact shading against the floor tile.

examples.what_to_look_at: Object-shadow treatment vs. floating objects

title: PixelLab has a dedicated pixel-UI generation endpoint
claim: PixelLab's generate-ui-v2 endpoint generates pixel-art UI elements (dialogue boxes, health bars, buttons) from a text description.
project_relevance: If we ever need in-game pixel UI chrome, this is the documented endpoint — but no craft/game source was found to validate style conventions for it.

title: CameraView enum has no dedicated isometric value
claim: The CameraView enum is exactly ["side", "low top-down", "high top-down"]; our 2:1 iso look must be approximated via low/high top-down, not a dedicated iso camera mode.
project_relevance: Sets expectations for hero generation: we're choosing the closer-matching top-down variant, not a true iso render — informs the view=='low top-down' vs 'high top-down' A/B test already run in hero v3.

title: Richer style-transfer fields exist but weren't used for hero v3
claim: style_description, reference_image / style_character_id, color_image / force_colors exist on other PixelLab endpoints (generate-with-style-v2, create-image-bitforge, transfer-outfit-v2, image-to-pixelart) but were not exercised by the create-character-v3 calls inspected for hero v3.
project_relevance: If we want tighter style consistency between hero and env art later, these are the documented levers to reach for — but doing so would spend additional generations, against the current trial-budget constraint.

title: Run /unzoom before feeding user art to any reference/style endpoint
claim: The docs explicitly state that upscaled pixel art confuses PixelLab's style/reference models, and running /unzoom first is 'the most common cause of disappointing output' if skipped.
project_relevance: Hard rule for any future workflow where we feed hand-drawn or scanned reference art into PixelLab for style matching.

title: PixelLab has a server-side reduce-colors endpoint as an alternative to local quantization
claim: POST /reduce-colors accepts a num_colors parameter to cap a generated image's palette server-side; our current pipeline instead quantizes locally (MEDIANCUT to 48 colours, binarized alpha).
project_relevance: Our local quantize_hero.py approach is functionally equivalent and avoids spending an extra generation call; no change recommended, but worth knowing the API alternative exists.

title: Hero v3 create-character-v3 request shape used in practice
claim: Actual hero v3 calls set description, image_size (88x88), view, seed, n_directions=8, no_background=true, outline='single color black outline', detail='medium detail', name — the full working parameter set for our pipeline.
project_relevance: This is the exact, verified baseline request shape for any future hero generation call, confirmed by direct inspection of our own call logs (not a public source, but ground truth for our pipeline).

title: create-tileset generates Wang tiles with matching edges
claim: POST /create-tileset produces connected Wang tilesets whose edges line up, intended for top-down maps and platformers.
project_relevance: A candidate tool for generating our floor/wall tile variants with guaranteed edge continuity, if we spend future generations on environment tiles rather than hand-drawing them.

title: Style can converge through solo iteration, not a formal pipeline
claim: Stardew Valley was developed solo by ConcernedApe through direct iteration rather than a formal art pipeline (source confirms solo development; it does not specify his prior pixel-art experience level or an exact iteration duration).
project_relevance: Scoping lesson for our small team: budget for iterative art passes over time rather than expecting one perfect pipeline up front.

title: Production method: Blender->pixel vs PixelLab vs hybrid
claim: Decision from the 2026-10-15 in-scene spike (hero v3 + 5 Blender->pixel assets composited at zoom 1 and zoom 2, exact integer-grid math, nearest-neighbour): KEEP the Blender->pixel pipeline as the structural foundation for Scene 01 (floors, walls, large built-ins) and run hero-facing props HYBRID (Blender geometry + hand-drawn detail pass). Do NOT drop the pipeline, and do NOT use it as the sole method for props the hero stands next to. Evidence for keep: (a) geometry is exact 2:1 64x32 with no shimmer and crisp pixels at both zooms; hero feet sit on the tile grid, no floating/clipping/draw-order bugs; (b) it beats the current PIL props (iso-engine/assets/props.png) on every visual axis in the side-by-side verdict - stair-stepped hard diagonals vs anti-aliased/fuzzy diagonals, coherent Scandi palette (scene01_palette_v2) vs incoherent earthy reds/yellows/grays, zero noise pixels vs stray specks; (c) cost is negligible - 5 assets in 8.9s total (floor_tile_oak 2.3s, wall_segment_2u 1.2s, bed_wall 2.7s, kitchen_corner 1.3s, sofa 1.4s) with a one-command deterministic rebuild in ~6s. Evidence for hybrid: 3-bucket face-normal toon shading on boxy primitives reads visibly flatter and lower-detail than the hero sprite in the in-scene composite - the ~10 hero-facing furniture items (bed, sofa, kitchen counter, fridge, TV console, lamp, plants, decor) need a hand-drawn detail pass (or PixelLab generate-with-style-v2 with the hero as style reference) over the Blender geometry.
project_relevance: Decides how the 23-item Scene 01 furniture list plus 2 floor variants and 5 wall segments get produced, and sets the per-asset cost baseline (~2s/asset, ~6s full rebuild) for future rooms. Independent QA parity score against the same assets runs on t_dd5f77f1; this item is the art-direction decision, not the QA verdict.
